question.text: Will Berkshire Hathaway increase its holdings of Alphabet stock in its Q3 2026 13F filing?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if the 13F [filing](https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1067983&owner=exclude) for Berkshire Hathaway, Inc., filed for the period ending 2026-09-30, reports the company holding greater than 105,979,600 shares of Alphabet, Inc.
question.fine_print: The number is summed across all Alphabet share classes and entries.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-13: EDGAR still shows the Q2 2026 13F-HR (filed 2026-08-14) as Berkshire's most recent 13F. The Q3 filing (period ending 2026-09-30) has not been posted yet. Earlier 13Fs were filed on 2026-05-15, 2026-02-17 and 2025-11-14. [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=1067983&type=13F&dateb=&owner=include&count=40)
- 2026-08-14: The Q2 13F showed 78,791,167 Class A plus 27,188,433 Class C shares, for 105,979,600 in total. That is exactly the question's threshold, so even a small net increase resolves Yes, and an unchanged position resolves No. [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3930796/berkshire-just-made-a-huge-alphabet-bet-should-you-follow)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The Q3 13F is due Monday, 2026-11-16. [PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/famous-investors-face-a-nov-16-holdings-deadline-while-recent-filings-fill-in-the-gap-302936096.html)
- I found no Form 4 or other disclosure of Alphabet trades by Berkshire in Q3. A Form 4 would not be expected anyway, because Berkshire owns far less than 10% of Alphabet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-12: A Yahoo preview, citing the Q3 10-Q filed 2026-11-07, says Berkshire bought about $2.4B of stocks and sold about $2.8B in Q3, a small net sale. It spent $9.6B on its own buybacks. These totals include holdings that 13Fs leave out, such as the Japanese trading houses. Alphabet is down about 18% since June 30. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/watch-berkshire-hathaway-files-13f-163542466.html)
- 2026-11-11: Berkshire bought about $27M of Sirius XM between Oct 30 and Nov 3, bringing its stake to 37.4%. This shows Abel is still making small buys. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/11/greg-abel-berkshire-hathaway-own-sirius-stock/)
- 2026-10-31: CNBC says the Alphabet stake peaked at about $40B in early August and had fallen to $29.6B. Barron's estimates Berkshire's cost basis at over $300 a share, "perhaps close to $320," so the position is under water. Berkshire also sold $69M of DaVita, a routine sale under its agreement to stay at or below 45%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/berkshire-ekes-out-some-new-highs-but-october-rally-stalls.html)
- 2026-07-15: Buffett told CNBC he personally started the Alphabet position. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/15/warren-buffett-tells-cnbc-he-initiated-berkshire-hathaways-investment-in-alphabet.html)
- 2026-06-01: Berkshire put $10B into Alphabet's private placement. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/01/berkshire-hathaway-alphabet-investment.html)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Share count by quarter:
  - Q3 2025: about 17.85M Class A shares (position opened). I am working from memory here and did not re-check the filing.
  - Q4 2025: I could not confirm the figure.
  - Q1 2026: 54,249,798 Class A plus 3,585,215 Class C, about 57.8M in total.
  - Q2 2026: about 106.0M, up 48.1M. About $10B came from the private placement and about $7B from open-market buying. [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/buffett-berkshire-alphabet-stock-q2-2026/), [Barchart](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3930796/berkshire-just-made-a-huge-alphabet-bet-should-you-follow)
- The trend is a share increase in every reported quarter since the position opened.
- Against that, total Q3 stock purchases were only about $2.4B. At Alphabet prices of roughly $250-320, that is at most about 8-9M shares even if all of it went to Alphabet. The 10-Q also shows a small net sale overall, so a large Alphabet addition in Q3 looks unlikely, though a small one is still possible.
- Historically, Berkshire usually holds a position steady for a quarter or more after a big build. It sometimes keeps buying (Apple in 2016-2018, Chubb, Occidental).
- Berkshire has sometimes asked the SEC for confidential treatment, which hides a building position from the 13F (e.g. Chubb and Alphabet in earlier filings). I found no mention of that for Q3.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets supplied with the question match it: they cover Massachusetts House races, Treasury holdings, US government stakes and similar.
- I found no analyst preview that specifically predicts Alphabet share changes in the Q3 13F. One earlier preview mentioned speculation about a new Microsoft position. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/08/14/berkshire-13f-what-to-expect-from-buffett-successors-latest-moves/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-16 (Monday): Berkshire's Q3 13F deadline. Berkshire usually files after the market closes on deadline day, which is before the expected resolution around 2026-11-17 00:00 UTC.
- The 13F will also show whether Berkshire filed a confidential-treatment request, which could hide Q3 Alphabet activity.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The Q3 2026 13F is due Monday 2026-11-16, and Berkshire normally files after the close that day, so the outcome should be known in about 3 days. For Yes, the filing for the period ending 2026-09-30 must report Alphabet Class A plus Class C shares, summed across all entries, strictly above 105,979,600. Even a one-share net increase counts.

(b) The status quo is No. An unchanged position equals the threshold exactly, and the threshold is not exceeded.

(c) Base rate: across all of Berkshire's large positions, the share count is unchanged in most quarters, so an increase happens perhaps 20-30% of the time. Positions that are actively being built, as Alphabet has been in every quarter checked, get added to again in the following quarter more often, perhaps 50-60% of the time. Blending the two gives a starting point of about 40%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The stake rose in every quarter checked: opened in Q3 2025, roughly tripled in Q1 2026, and up 83% in Q2 2026 (about $7B of that was open-market buying).
- Buffett publicly championed the stake (2026-07-15), which signals high conviction.
- Berkshire still made $2.4B of gross equity purchases in Q3 (10-Q filed 2026-11-07), and Alphabet is a plausible destination for some of that money.

Evidence for No:
- Q3 was a net sale overall ($2.4B bought, $2.8B sold), so there was little capacity for a sizable add.
- Alphabet peaked in early August, which made Q3 a costly time to buy.
- Berkshire often pauses after a large build-up, and the Q2 jump was huge.
- The $2.4B could have gone to the Japanese trading houses or other names.
- A confidential-treatment request could hide any additions from this filing.
- A small trim of the minor Class A sub-entries would also resolve No.

(e) No scenario: Berkshire digests the Q2 build. The $2.4B goes to the trading houses, Sirius XM, Domino's and similar names, the Alphabet shares are unchanged at 105,979,600, and the question resolves No.

Yes scenario: Abel or Buffett keeps accumulating during the July-September dips, using $1-2B of the gross purchases to add about 5M shares, and the 13F shows about 111M shares.

(f) I start at about 40%. I move down a few points because the overall net-selling quarter and the high Q3 prices make continued buying less likely, and because of the small chance of confidential treatment. I don't go lower, because the strong accumulation trend and the unexplained $2.4B of purchases keep Yes very plausible.

Probability: 36%

(a) The Q3 2026 13F is due Monday 2026-11-16, and Berkshire usually files after the close that day. The outcome should be known in about 3 days, before resolution around 2026-11-17 00:00 UTC. Yes requires the summed Alphabet Class A and Class C shares across all entries to be strictly greater than 105,979,600, the exact Q2 total.

(b) Status quo: an unchanged position resolves No. That is the default for a large Berkshire holding right after a big build.

(c) Base rate: Berkshire's large positions stay unchanged or shrink in most quarters, and it was a net seller in 15 of the last 16 quarters. Across Berkshire holdings in general, roughly 20-30% show an increase in any given quarter. The Alphabet position specifically has grown in every quarter I could check, which pushes the reference class higher, to about 40-50% for an actively built position. I start at about 35%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The stake grew in Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026, by 48M shares in Q2 alone.
- Buffett personally backs the position (2026-07-15).
- Berkshire still made $2.4B of gross stock purchases in Q3, and some of that could have gone to Alphabet.
- Small subsidiary-manager entries, such as the 16,700-share line, can drift slightly upward. Any net increase counts.

Evidence for No:
- The Q3 10-Q (2026-11-07) shows only $2.4B of purchases against $2.8B of sales, a net sale. The purchases include non-13F holdings.
- Alphabet traded near its peak during Q3. The stake was worth about $40B in early August (CNBC 2026-10-31), and Berkshire's estimated cost basis is about $320. Buying more at those prices is less Berkshire-like.
- After a $17B build in one quarter, a pause is typical.
- Kingswell's Q3 review notes no Alphabet trades.
- A confidential-treatment filing would hide any additions.

(e) No scenario: Berkshire holds its 105,979,600 shares flat in Q3, and the $2.4B of purchases went to Japanese trading houses, other holdings or small names. The filing shows an identical count.
Yes scenario: Abel keeps averaging into Alphabet with $1-2B of the Q3 purchases, or a subsidiary manager adds a few thousand shares. The total edges above the threshold.

(f) The tiny gross buying budget and the net selling pull me down from about 35%. The tiny required increase and the active build trend partly offset that. I settle near 27%.

Probability: 27%

(a) Berkshire's Q3 2026 13F is due Monday 2026-11-16 and will probably be filed after the close that day, roughly 3 days from now and before resolution around 2026-11-17 00:00 UTC. For Yes, the summed Alphabet Class A and Class C shares across all entries must be strictly greater than 105,979,600, the exact Q2 total. Any net purchase, however small, resolves Yes.
